hypotheses: A/B/C ARCHITECTURE COMPARISON — A is the no-build control: existing Navigator One design seed, existing owner outputs and paper/science controls, with no new component. Correctness and provenance remain whatever the owners can demonstrate; privacy adds no new surface; realism remains limited to existing evidence. No new processing stage, dependency or maintenance seam. Existing defects, latency and operating costs are UNKNOWN. A is the only defensible comparison posture on this packet, not proof that the incumbent is sufficient.

B is the minimal clean-room alternative to test: project existing immutable outputs into a read-only product view; consider a pure paper validator or reconciler only for a demonstrated owner gap. Correctness and provenance could improve through explicit refusals, evidence binding and replay checks; privacy must remain bounded by the existing output contract. Realism cannot exceed the input evidence. Extra validation cost, receipt latency, schema complexity and maintenance drift are liabilities to measure. Drop B if A already passes, if B merely relocates the same logic, or if B requires a new producer, runtime, data route or privilege.

C is a component comparison, not full-stack adoption. A narrowly bounded presentation dependency is testable only if B cannot meet a demonstrated need and the exact revision, license, notices, dependency inventory and privacy behavior are cleared. Check output fidelity and attribution for correctness/provenance, isolation for privacy, and incremental footprint, latency, operational and upgrade costs for burden. A chart library adds no execution realism; a simulation engine adds no observable realism without sufficiently granular evidence. C must beat B on the documented gap without losing owner control. Matching engines remain deferred. No measured scores are available for A, B or C.

TOP 10 CLEAN-ROOM PRIMITIVES — 1. Point-in-time identity and availability. Compare with Alpha #228 and the existing E1/E1X controls, not a new scanner. Bind exact chain, contract address and pool to source revision, event time and first usable availability; preserve omissions and disagreement. Acceptance: adding a later correction or a pre-cutoff event that only became available after cutoff leaves the original decision unchanged; same ticker on a different chain or pool cannot be joined. A correctly identified, timely twin remains usable. Measure leakage and identity errors on a newly unverified lane only; depend on the incumbent identity contract and frozen versions.

2. Scoped, expiring quote evidence. Compare with A's quote/receipt contract and M3's narrower cache observation. Test an envelope for side, chain, instrument, pool or route, raw size and units, evidence class, issuer, observation/availability/expiry, scope and immutable digest. Expired, wrong-size, wrong-scope and restarted-cache fixtures must not receive new paper credit; the timely matching twin remains eligible. Measure invalid admissions, valid-case refusals and lookup/validation burden. Depend on a trusted cutoff and existing freshness policy; do not invent a TTL or assume a cache hit renews it.

3. Evidence-tiered paper liquidation. Compare with A and the M1 booking-versus-reset distinction. A bid-side quote covering the quantity at the decision cutoff can support only a conditional paper result, not a guaranteed execution. Test full size, partial evidence, wrong side, indicative marks and outage. Partial evidence must not credit the remainder as sold; a valid full-size twin should pass if otherwise eligible. Disclose fees, gas conversion, spread, slippage, latency and MEV assumptions separately where observable, without double counting amounts already in the quote. Measure unsupported credited quantity and cost error. Depend on P2 and size-specific exit evidence.

4. Integer reconciliation and typed marks. Compare with A's paper book; M1 and M4 motivate the tests, not a code port. Test raw integer amounts, independently evidenced decimals and currency conversions, and the owner's declared rounding. A zero-quantity booking, absent decimals, unknown fee conversion, duplicate partial or reset-at-mark must not create realized proceeds. Valid independent partials and the final close must reconcile quantity, fees, reservations and cash in their declared units. Measure unit-conservation violations and mark-as-fill errors. Depend on the existing paper ledger and unit contract.

5. Atomic reservation across paper strategies. Compare with A's paper accounting and the #1133 portfolio boundary. Under one frozen simulation scope, dispatch two individually eligible intents that cannot both fit the existing simulated constraints. An atomic check and reservation must prevent double allocation; two independently affordable controls must not be spuriously blocked. Verify that unresolved aggregate state does not become available cash or known diversification. Measure oversubscription, false blocks and reconciliation errors. Depend on the incumbent paper state owner and existing policy; no real cash, holdings, budget or limit changes.

6. Independent decision and refusal receipt. Compare with the September protocol principle and existing delegation/receipt owners. A typed proposal cannot authorize itself. Test that untrusted free text, stop state, missing evidence and an unavailable decision service create accountable non-admission, not silent disappearance or a permission grant. A valid paper control should produce a complete decision and receipt. Measure dispositions per attempted event, reason completeness and unauthorized capability exposure. Depend on the existing policy owner and review evidence for the receipt boundary; no model tool may sign or execute.

7. Deterministic replay and unknown-commit recovery. Compare with A's recovery contract; M2 demonstrates local FIFO only and M6 is documentary. Test interruptions on either side of a simulated commit, duplicate and out-of-order deliveries, a conflicting payload under one intent key, and a source reorg. Require stable authoritative results for exact duplicates, no repeated debit or fill, and an explicit unresolved state rather than blind replay when commit status cannot be proved. A distinct valid child fill remains admissible. Measure state/receipt differences on identical frozen traces and false quarantine on valid controls. Depend on P5, P6 and an owner-provided commit boundary.

8. Least-privilege projection and UNKNOWN balances. Compare with the existing portfolio view and three-plane boundary. Test an unavailable balance against an independently attested zero; they must render differently. With synthetic identifiers, verify that logs, notices and receipts cannot disclose out-of-scope identifiers or provider values, and that the projection exposes no signer, transfer or analytics capability. Measure disclosure failures and UNKNOWN-to-zero errors. Depend on existing public-safe schemas; no wallet integration. This is a prerequisite across B, not a feature to defer until UI review.

9. Complete attempt and trial accounting. Compare with #1557, the Research Lab owner and E1/E1X, not a replacement ledger. Preserve proposal-time trial N separately from observed opportunities, paper intents and receipt attempts; keep rejected, abandoned, failed, timed-out and missing cases in their relevant denominators. A survivor-only filter and a planted future-data join should fail audit; an unchanged A/A trace and valid point-in-time prefix should not. Measure lost attempts, leakage and rewrites. Depend on evidence that the existing controls apply to the candidate cohort.

10. Owner-backed UX that explains refusal without inventing results. Compare with the current Navigator One seed and owner views, when available. Give reviewers matched fixtures with stale data, source disagreement, an administrative mark, a paper result and a forecast with a missing actual. Test interpretation accuracy, time to locate the evidence, keyboard/screen-reader use and duplicate notices; a complete source-backed case must remain easy to find. Depend on P1, P6 and P8. Prefer a projection of existing receipts; reject the design if it needs a duplicate source or merely shifts ambiguity to a tooltip.

TYPED PAPER CONTRACT TO TEST — Observation carries schema and source revisions, exact identity, evidence references, event/availability clocks, omissions and conflicts. PaperIntent carries a stable scoped ID, input/quote references and digest, side, raw quantity, simulation scope and cutoff; it contains no signable payload. IndependentDecision binds the policy revision and paper-book version and yields ALLOW_PAPER, DENY or UNKNOWN with reason codes. PaperReceipt binds the disposition, input/state digests, clock and replay lineage, simulated reservation and ledger deltas with units, and cost/evidence class. Keep quote-backed simulation, administrative mark and observed market actual distinct. UNKNOWN is not zero, consent, or a completed transaction.

PAPER FAILURE INVARIANT TO TEST — Validate evidence identity, scope, freshness and availability at the frozen decision cutoff; if the relevant clocks or policy are missing, no mutation or credit. Within an authorized simulator, compare the expected book revision and treat reservation, applicable quote use, paper deltas and the authoritative receipt as one logical commit. Exact replay returns the existing receipt; same key with different content is a conflict. Quote consumption is scoped to the simulation, not global across independent A/B arms. Recovered or revised state links to prior receipts without rewriting them. Demonstrate pre-commit failure, commit-before-acknowledgment and unresolved-commit controls without a runtime or real wallet.

UX INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE TO TEST — Today: owner publications, freshness, gaps and disagreements. Alpha: exact chain/contract/pool and evidence for admission or refusal, never a new scan. Desk: paper attempts, quote coverage, costs and skip reasons; no execution controls. Portfolio: separate owner valuations from simulation and administrative marks; distinguish available, reserved, zero and unavailable. Lab: frozen cohorts, trial history, forecast issue time/horizon/units and observed actuals. Keep the existing blue-forecast/green-actual distinction with text/pattern labels and visible gaps, never interpolate or overwrite a frozen forecast. Compare desktop list-plus-detail with mobile summary cards and accessible drilldown on synthetic fixtures. Test passive, deduplicated freshness/conflict/recovery notices from existing outputs; no new background alerts, private identifiers or trade prompts.

SCIENTIFIC TEST — Freeze the eligible opportunity set and decision cutoffs before outcomes, including refusals, unavailable inputs, backfills and no-receipt cases. Pair A and B by opportunity ID on the same evidence tape and policy; use identical A/A as a negative control. Report the disposition-transition matrix, reason-only changes and receipt coverage. If d paired dispositions differ, p have both dispositions, and u of N frozen opportunities lack a pair, report d/p where defined and the cohort bounds d/N to (d+u)/N where N is known. Explicit UNKNOWN is a recorded decision; absent receipts are missing, not denials. Stratify by source, outage, revision and state/restart case. These are definitions for a future matched test, not packet estimates.

COST AND ABLATION TEST — Independent adjudication uses the evidence and policy legitimately available at the cutoff. An unsupported admission or credit is an engineering false positive; denying an independently admissible case is an engineering false negative. A correct refusal on missing evidence is not a hindsight error. Report counts and rates on their labeled denominators, plus unlabeled coverage. Separate invalid simulated credits, reservation errors and review/recovery time from economic cost. Monetize only with independently defensible quantities and consistently denominated costs; value forgone feasible opportunities, including losing ones, against a fixed no-admission counterfactual on sealed after-cost evidence, with uncertainty and no favorable censoring. Compare paired B-minus-A differences by metric and cost unit, not an invented weighted score. Isolate quote binding, reservation/recovery and UI projection one at a time so a cosmetic improvement cannot mask lost coverage.

KNOWLEDGE-TIME AND SCIENCE SENSITIVITY TEST — Compare decisions on original availability-frozen versions versus later corrections/backfills, and separately on identical frozen inputs across designs. Record receipt/source revision, clocks and reason changes so data revisions are not mistaken for policy improvements. Reuse right-truncation and declared warm-up controls where applicable, and blind adjudicators to outcomes and prior verdicts. Freeze the trial denominator and holdout before evaluation; account for dependence across time and sources. If a delegation comparison later clears existing gates, compare one model with bounded specialists on the same opportunities, information, policy and existing cost/time constraints, including failed handoffs and review burden. Synthetic success tests engineering behavior only. No Round 3 access, scoring or economic inference.
